name: After Action Review
use_case: A structured debrief of one specific completed event built on four questions: what did we expect to happen, what actually happened, why did those differ, and what will we do differently next time. Best used immediately after a discrete event such as a launch, an incident response, an exercise or a customer escalation, when the goal is to convert that single episode into transferable lessons while recollection is still accurate.
strengths: anchored on one event, so it stays concrete and evidence-based
the expected-versus-actual gap is where the real learning sits
works across ranks when the facilitator suspends hierarchy
short enough to run while memories are fresh
weaknesses: covers a single event, so it misses slow-building systemic patterns
degrades into blame assignment without disciplined facilitation
loses accuracy the longer it is postponed, as recollection gives way to reconstruction
lessons evaporate unless someone owns carrying them to the next event
use_cases: A civil protection agency has just run a large emergency exercise with several services and needs to capture where the plan held and where it broke down before everyone disperses.
A school has carried out its first evacuation or lockdown drill of the year, and staff want to compare what the emergency plan said with what actually happened in the building.
The outage is over and service is restored; the on-call engineers and support staff want to walk through how the response unfolded against the runbook while it is fresh.
A development programme has finished a field distribution or training round, and partner staff want lessons written down for colleagues planning similar activities elsewhere.
